absent: Full migrate-scanner and free-scanner algorithms, isolation and suitability predicates, and deferral timing outside the routed tails.
Buddy allocator, slab, reclaim, LRU and capture allocation paths beyond the drain and guard hooks shown.
Exact lock ordering, sleep contexts and concurrency guarantees for zone, node and pool structures.
Fragmentation scoring, proactive tuning, watermark checks and event accounting definitions.
Sysctl and sysfs permission handling, error propagation and device lifecycle beyond the shown handlers.

findings.text: Provides zonelist-wide direct compaction driver that callers invoke with allocation context, priority and capture state; it walks candidate zones, skips ineligible or deferred ones, and reports an aggregate outcome favoring success.

Exposes background compaction controls for waking the per-node thread with coalesced demand, starting and stopping that thread during memory online handling, and adding or removing the per-node compaction attribute.
Offers a zone-scoped flush of cached pages held on processors, delegating to a shared drain routine in non-forced mode.
Provides guard marking helpers that test an order threshold before flagging a block and that clear the marking on release.
Provides tiny wrappers that forward page pointer plus numeric arguments to tracing for reference lifecycle events such as set, modify, conditional modify, freeze and unfreeze.

Free element pairs a linkage field with a device address. Page header pairs list linkage with virtual and device addresses for one chunk. Pool descriptor tracks population and activity counts, cached element, device association, sizing and boundary values, node preference and fixed label storage; page collection linkage is page_list, registry linkage is pools, exclusion is lock and label storage is name, described here out of source order.

Serializes pool directory enumeration for reporting with a dedicated mutex, holding it while walking the device pool set and emitting one summary line per pool plus a header, then releasing before returning the accumulated length.
Declares a second mutex named for registry protection; the routed window shows only its definition, with no use site visible.

Coordinates cache flushing with a global drain mutex that is tried opportunistically for whole-system flushes but waited upon for zone-specific requests, combined with per-cache spin protection around count sampling and bulk release in batches derived from configured batch scale.

Derives a mobility grouping from allocation flags by shifting the masked mobility bits, with compile-time checks tying flag positions to expected groups and a global disable switch forcing all requests to the unmovable group.

Builds a zone-scoped compaction request from caller order, mask and zone limit, selecting light synchronous migration except for asynchronous priority, marking the request direct, and enabling whole-zone and hint-ignoring scans only at the lowest priority level.

After each scan cycle the zone worker treats an observed captured page as immediate success, drains per-processor additions once migration crosses an aligned block boundary, and on exit releases accumulated free pages, rewinds the cached free restart backward-only to a block start, then accounts scanned totals before returning.

Iterates zonelist candidates publishing the current zone to capture state, skipping cpuset-excluded and deferred zones while remembering deferral, accumulating the best status seen, resetting deferral on success, applying deferral on complete or partially skipped synchronous attempts, and aborting remaining zones on rescheduling need in asynchronous mode or on a fatal signal.

Background thread sleeps with a default period that becomes indefinite when proactive control is disabled, runs demand work under memory-pressure accounting when woken for explicit requests, otherwise evaluates fragmentation and runs proactive sweeps with backoff when no progress occurs, finally clearing any manual trigger before sleeping again.

Demand worker walks zones up to the requested limit, ignoring unpopulated and deferred zones and those already suitable, compacting each remaining zone, resetting deferral on success and draining cached pages plus deferring on partial or complete outcomes, then clears request state only when the observed demand does not exceed what was just processed.

Manual compaction is reachable through a write-only memory control that compacts all online nodes when set to one, a proactive intensity control that wakes per-node threads on nonzero writes, a per-node sysfs attribute that compacts the selected online node after flushing queued additions, and boot registration that starts threads and installs the control table, including a wrapper that warns once on real-time builds when a value actually changes.

Debug allocation controls include early boot parsing for enabling page-allocation checking and a separate order threshold parser that rejects missing, malformed or oversized values with an error while accepting and announcing valid settings. Related key and threshold objects are declared alongside.

Guard marking applies only below a configured minimum order, setting a guard flag, initializing list linkage and recording order in private storage, returning whether marking occurred; clearing removes the flag and zeroes private storage without consulting zone or order beyond the call signature.

Pool reporting produces a versioned header followed by one line per pool summarizing activity and capacity; the routine holds no statistics beyond current counts and sizes already stored in the descriptor.

Compaction paths check for fatal signals and asynchronous rescheduling needs to abort promptly, assert that no migration list entries remain at zone exit and that released free runs are non-empty, and move cached restart positions only backward to avoid skipping pages freed late.

Virtual-memory controls expose compact_memory as write-only, plus compaction_proactiveness bounded zero to one hundred, extfrag_threshold bounded zero to one thousand, and compact_unevictable_allowed bounded zero to one with a real-time change warning handler.
Pool debug flag carries value one; trace point creation is enabled in its translation unit.

Node sweep iterates all zone indices, skipping unpopulated zones and aborting with an interrupt error on fatal signal, configuring light synchronous migration for proactive passes and full synchronous migration otherwise while always ignoring skip hints and scanning whole zones.

Wake requests ignore order zero, coalesce by retaining the maximum order and tightest zone limit seen, avoid waking without a sleeper or when no zone still needs work, and otherwise emit a wake event and signal the node wait queue.

Drain preparation builds a processor set by inspecting cached counts, forcing inclusion for all online processors when requested, otherwise including only those with non-empty caches for the target zone or for any populated zone, then invokes zone-scoped or global flushing per selected processor.
